measurement_groups.paper_use: Change in walking speed from baseline to the participant’s last follow-up wave, up to 12 years later. HRS walking speed was assessed by asking participants to walk at normal speed, using walking devices if helpful, over 8.21 feet / 2.5 meters, with two trials at baseline and follow-up waves. Speed was calculated as distance divided by time; the analysis used the faster of the two trials to assess maximum capability. Baseline walking speed was reported in cm/s. For the primary binary outcome, participants were coded 1 if last-follow-up walking speed exceeded baseline walking speed and 0 if they stayed the same or walked slower.

observable_indicators: one point for each correct subtraction
summed working memory score across waves
measurement_groups.paper_use: Telephone Interview for Cognitive Status-27 seven subtraction task. observable_indicators: Immediate recall of 10 nouns, contributing up to 10 points

measurement_groups.paper_use: Cognitive function was scored with the 27-point Langa-Weir Classification Scale using HRS cognitive tests. measurement_groups.paper_use: Respiratory sarcopenia was defined as the co-occurrence of low respiratory muscle strength and low muscle mass. In HRS, low respiratory muscle strength was PEFR below sex-specific cohort thresholds: <5.46 L/s for males and <3.76 L/s for females. Low muscle mass was height-adjusted appendicular skeletal muscle mass index below sex-specific 20th-percentile thresholds: ASM/height² <7.58 kg/m² for males and <5.80 kg/m² for females. HRS ASM was not directly measured; it was predicted as ASM = 0.485 × 0.998^age × 0.814^[1 for female, 0 for male] × 1.006^height in cm × weight in kg^0.680. measurement_groups.paper_use: Respondents’ repeated Langa-Weir cognition scores from the 2012–2020 HRS surveys were used to estimate age-based group-based trajectories. measurement_groups.measurement: Incident cognitive impairment
observable_indicators: Langa-Weir Classification Scale score less than 12
measurement_groups.paper_use: Cognitive function assessed at each wave using the 27-item Langa-Weir Classification Scale, range 0-27, based on immediate and delayed 10-noun recall, serial 7 subtraction, and backward counting from 20. Cognitive impairment was coded yes/no as a score less than 12. Participants with baseline cognitive impairment, Alzheimer’s disease, or dementia were excluded so the survival outcome captures development of impairment over follow-up.

measurement_groups.paper_use: Self-reported sensory loss was measured in each HRS wave from 1998 through 2006 and summarized cumulatively. Hearing loss was coded present when self-rated hearing, using a hearing aid as usual, was “fair” or “poor”; other responses were no hearing loss. Vision loss was coded present when any of three vision questions—overall eyesight, distance eyesight, or near eyesight, using glasses/corrective lenses as usual—was “fair,” “poor,” or “legally blind”; other responses were no vision loss. Dual sensory loss was having both hearing and vision loss in the same wave; any sensory loss was having either hearing or vision loss in the same wave. Cumulative measures were analyzed as continuous counts and categorical groups: never, 1 time point, 2 time points, and ≥3 time points. CHL, CVL, and CDSL ranged from 0 to 5; the paper states CASL ranged from 0 to 10.

measurement_groups.measurement: Cognitive function and cognitive decline
measurement_groups.paper_use: Cognitive function was measured with the TICS-m cognitive battery. Global cognition was a 0–27 score summing memory and executive function domains. Memory combined immediate word recall (0–10) and delayed word recall (0–10). Executive function combined serial 7 subtraction (0–5) and backward counting (0–2). Higher scores indicated better cognition. Domain z-scores were calculated, and global cognition z-score was re-standardized as the mean of the two domain z-scores using 2004 baseline mean and SD for all subsequent years. Decline was assessed as longitudinal change in global cognition, memory, and executive function z-scores from 2004 through 2020.

observable_indicators: Frequency of vigorous sports or activities

measurement_groups.paper_use: Physical activity was self-reported separately for vigorous, moderate, and light/mild activity frequency. Responses for each intensity were coded from 0 to 4, weighted by intensity-specific MET-related weights, summed into total MET-PA, and then accumulated using area under the curve with the trapezoid rule. For the duration analysis, cumulative PA was calculated over successively longer engagement periods: 2-year, 4-year, 6-year, and 8-year accumulation windows from baseline, and one-SD increments in those cPA measures were compared for their association with later cognitive decline.

measurement_groups.measurement: Memory trajectory
observable_indicators: Delayed recall of the same 10 nouns after approximately 5 minutes
measurement_groups.paper_use: Memory was measured at three time points using immediate and delayed word-recall tasks. Respondents heard a list of 10 nouns, immediately recalled as many as possible, and after about 5 minutes recalled the nouns again. The memory score summed correct words from immediate and delayed recall, yielding a 0–20 score; higher scores indicated better memory. The analysis modeled memory trajectories across T1, T2, and T3 with a latent growth curve, with the intercept representing T3 memory and the slope representing linear change over the 8-year period.

measurement_groups.measurement: Long-term visit-to-visit resting heart rate variability
observable_indicators: three seated resting heart-rate measurements per wave
average of three valid heart-rate measurements at each wave
within-person mean resting heart rate across visits
within-person standard deviation of resting heart rate across visits
variability independent of the mean score
measurement_groups.paper_use: Resting heart rate was measured at each HRS wave from 2006 through 2018 as the average of three valid seated heart-rate measurements taken 45–60 seconds apart by trained interviewers using an Omron monitor. Long-term RHRV was defined as intraindividual variability in resting heart rate across three or more visits. The main exposure was variability independent of the mean (VIM), calculated as 100 × SD / mean^beta, where beta is from the regression of ln(SD) on ln(mean). Higher VIM indicates greater visit-to-visit resting heart-rate variability. CV and ARV were calculated only for sensitivity analyses.

measurement_groups.measurement: Cognitive functioning over repeated visits
measurement_groups.paper_use: Cognitive function was measured biennially at each wave using questionnaire-based tests covering memory, orientation, and executive function. Memory was assessed with immediate and delayed word recall. Orientation was assessed by questions about the test date/time, including year, month, day, and day of the week. Executive function in HRS included serial 7s subtraction and backward counting from 20. Higher scores indicated better performance. The paper defined global cognitive function as the sum of scores across memory, orientation, and executive-function dimensions and analyzed global and domain-specific cognitive function as z scores.

measurement_groups.measurement: High-risk inflammation markers from venous blood
measurement_groups.paper_use: Six separate dichotomous high-risk inflammation indicators were created for CRP and five cytokine biomarkers from the 2016 Venous Blood Study. For CRP, IL-6, IL-10, and TNFR1, high risk was defined as values in the upper quartile after top-coding at the 99th percentile; for IL-1RA and TGF-Beta, high risk was defined as values in the lowest quartile after bottom-coding at the 1st percentile. Reported non-standardized cutoffs were: CRP ≥ 5.02 mg/L; IL-6 ≥ 5.98 pg/mL; IL-10 ≥ 4.26 pg/mL; IL-1RA ≤ 366.03 pg/mL; TNFR1 ≥ 1,964.57 pg/mL; TGF-Beta ≤ 38,811.64 pg/mL. Each marker was modeled separately as high-risk = 1 versus lower-risk = 0.
